results.title: Coefficients of the Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U_n \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ denote the $n$-th Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind, and let $k \le n$ be natural numbers. If $n$ and $k$ have the same parity, the coefficient of $x^k$ in $U_n$ is $(-1)^{(n-k)/2} \sum_{i=0}^{k} \binom{(n+k)/2}{i} \binom{(n+k)/2 - i}{(n-k)/2}$; otherwise it is $0$.

results.title: Modified Chebyshev base polynomials of the second kind
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a commutative ring $R$ and $r, s \in R$, the polynomials $P_n \in R[x]$, $n \ge 0$, are defined by $P_0 = 1$, $P_1 = x - r$ and $P_{n+2} = (x - r) P_{n+1} - s P_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.

results.title: Generalized Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a commutative ring $R$ and $r, s, \lambda, \mu \in R$, let $P_n \in R[x]$ be the modified Chebyshev base polynomials with parameters $r, s$. The polynomials $Q_n \in R[x]$ are defined by $Q_0 = 1$, $Q_1 = P_1 - \lambda P_0$ and $Q_{n+2} = P_{n+2} - \lambda P_{n+1} - \mu P_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.

results.title: Three-term recurrence for generalized Chebyshev polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a commutative ring $R$, all $r, s, \lambda, \mu \in R$ and every $n \ge 0$, the generalized Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind $Q_n \in R[x]$ with parameters $r, s, \lambda, \mu$ satisfy $Q_{n+3} = (x - r) Q_{n+2} - s Q_{n+1}$.

results.summary: For a number field $K$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ and a height-one prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$, this is $\mathfrak p$ regarded as a fractional ideal of $K$; it is nonzero, hence a unit in the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$.

results.title: Factorization of a prime of a number field

results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be a height-one prime of $\mathcal O_K$. results.title: Primes not dividing the modulus are coprime to it

results.title: Central Erdős layer estimate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 512$ be a natural number and $N = 2n + 2$. For a natural number $x$ write $x\#$ for the primorial of $x$, the product of all primes $p \le x$, and let $L = \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$. Then $n \cdot \lfloor N/3 \rfloor\# \cdot \prod_{m=2}^{L} \lfloor N^{1/m} \rfloor\# < 4^n$.

results.title: Power-of-four bound for the Erdős layer product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $r$ be natural numbers. For a natural number $x$ write $x\#$ for the primorial of $x$, the product of all primes $p \le x$. Let $L = \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$, with $L = 0$ when $N = 0$, and let $P = 1$ if $L = 0$ and $P = r\# \cdot \prod_{m=2}^{L} \lfloor N^{1/m} \rfloor\#$ if $L \ge 1$. Then $P \le 4^{r + \lfloor \sqrt{N} \rfloor L}$.

results.title: Three-layer power-of-four bound for the Erdős layer product

results.title: $S$-Diophantine tuples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers. A finite set $s$ of natural numbers is an $S$-Diophantine tuple if all its elements are positive and, for all distinct $a, b \in s$, every prime factor of $ab + 1$ lies in $S$. A tuple $(a_1, \dots, a_m)$ of distinct positive integers is encoded by the set of its entries, which has $m$ elements.

results.title: Convergent denominators as continuants
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence of natural numbers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$, its convergent denominators $q_0, q_1, q_2, \dots$ are the natural numbers defined by $q_0 = 1$, $q_1 = a_1$ and $q_{i+2} = a_{i+2} q_{i+1} + q_i$ for $i \ge 0$. They are the denominators of the convergents of $[a_0; a_1, a_2, \dots]$, and $q_i$ is the continuant $K(a_1, \dots, a_i)$; the term $a_0$ is never used.

results.title: Perfect graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite simple graph $G$ is perfect if, for every set $S$ of its vertices, the induced subgraph $G[S]$ has chromatic number equal to its clique number, the largest size of a clique in $G[S]$.

results.title: Gasparian's condition (P)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite simple graph $G$ satisfies condition (P) if, for every set $S$ of its vertices, the induced subgraph $G[S]$, with independence number $\alpha(G[S])$ and clique number $\omega(G[S])$, satisfies $|S| \le \alpha(G[S]) \cdot \omega(G[S])$.

results.title: Perfect graphs satisfy condition (P)
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Weak perfect graph theorem

results.title: Lovász's weak perfect graph theorem
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Adjacency-matrix graph instance
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An instance consists of a natural number $n$ and a Boolean $n \times n$ matrix $A$ with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, read as the adjacency matrix of a graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$. The matrix is arbitrary; symmetry and the absence of loops are imposed separately by the validity condition.

results.title: Valid adjacency-matrix instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance with $n$ vertices and adjacency matrix $A$ is valid when $A$ is symmetric, that is, $A_{yx}$ is true whenever $A_{xy}$ is true, and has no loops, that is, $A_{xx}$ is false for every vertex $x$.

results.title: Graph of a valid instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A valid instance with $n$ vertices and adjacency matrix $A$ determines the simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which vertices $x$ and $y$ are adjacent exactly when $A_{xy}$ is true.

results.title: The perfect-graph decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem on bitstrings that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the bitstring encoding of adjacency-matrix instances, to a valid instance whose graph is perfect. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance, or decode to an invalid one, are rejected.

results.title: At-least-one literals of a cell
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $g, B \in \mathbb{N}$, the list of the $g$ positive literals on the variables $v_B, v_{B+1}, \dots, v_{B+g-1}$, in this order, each given as the pair of its variable index and the sign true; these are the literals of the clause $v_B \lor \dots \lor v_{B+g-1}$.

results.title: At-most-one literals for a pair
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $B, x, y \in \mathbb{N}$, the two-element list of the negative literals on the variables $v_{B+x}$ and $v_{B+y}$, in this order, each given as the pair of its variable index and the sign false; these are the literals of the clause $\neg v_{B+x} \lor \neg v_{B+y}$. It is used for pairs $x < y$.

results.title: At-most-one clauses of the first rows of a cell
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $V$, $B$ and $y$, write $p_i$ for the variable with index $i$. This is the CNF formula listing, for $y' = 0, 1, \dots, y - 1$ in turn and within each for $x = 0, 1, \dots, y' - 1$ in turn, the dense clause over $V$ variables built from the literals $\lnot p_{B + x}$ and $\lnot p_{B + y'}$: its slot $i < V$ holds the literal on $p_i$ if there is one and is empty otherwise.

results.title: One-hot clauses of a cell
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $g, V, B \in \mathbb{N}$, the CNF formula whose first clause is the at-least-one clause $v_B \lor \dots \lor v_{B+g-1}$ and whose remaining clauses are the at-most-one clauses $\neg v_{B+x} \lor \neg v_{B+y}$ for $x < y < g$, ordered by $y$ and then by $x$. Each clause is written densely over the $V$ variables $v_0, \dots, v_{V-1}$; literals on variables of index at least $V$ are dropped.

results.title: Pedigree
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A pedigree on the individuals `Fin n`, numbered so that parents precede their children (every finite pedigree, a finite DAG, has such a numbering). `parents i = some g` means that `g 0` is the father and `g 1` the mother of `i`; `parents i = none` means that `i` is a founder. Founders are unrelated and not inbred (their `2 n_F` gene copies are distinct).

results.title: Parent relation in a pedigree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `a` is a parent of `b`.

results.title: Ancestor relation in a pedigree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `a` is an ancestor of `b` (a parent, a parent of a parent, …).

results.title: Pedigree without selfing
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: No individual is the offspring of a selfing (father ≠ mother), as in Wright's setting of a bisexual population.

results.title: Gene-dropping outcome
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A gene-dropping outcome: `ω i k` is the Mendelian coin of the copy `(i, k)` (`k = 0` the paternal copy, `k = 1` the maternal copy), saying which copy (`0` or `1`) of the parent `g k` of `i` it inherits. Under gene dropping all `4 ^ n` outcomes are equally likely.

results.title: Founder origin of a gene copy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The founder copy from which the gene copy `c = (i, k)` descends under the gene-dropping outcome `ω`: a founder copy is its own origin; a copy of a non-founder descends from the copy `ω i k` of its parent `g k`.

results.title: Probability of identity by descent under gene dropping
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The probability, under gene dropping (independent fair Mendelian coins), that the gene copies `c` and `d` are identical by descent, i.e. descend from the same founder copy.

results.title: Kinship coefficient under gene dropping
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The kinship (coancestry) coefficient under gene dropping: the probability that a copy drawn at random from `i` and a copy drawn at random from `j` are identical by descent.

results.title: Inbreeding coefficient under gene dropping
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The inbreeding coefficient under gene dropping: the probability that the two copies of `i` are identical by descent.

results.title: Kinship coefficient by Malécot's recursion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The kinship coefficient by Malécot's recursion, computed in the order of the numbering (the tabular method): for `i < j`, `φ i j = (φ i f + φ i m) / 2` with `f, m` the parents of `j` and `φ i j = 0` if `j` is a founder; `φ i i = (1 + φ f m) / 2` with `f, m` the parents of `i` and `φ i i = 1 / 2` for a founder; symmetric for `j < i`.

results.title: Inbreeding coefficient by Malécot's recursion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The inbreeding coefficient by Malécot's recursion: `F i = φ f m` for the parents `f, m` of `i`, and `F i = 0` for a founder.

results.title: Tabular kinship when the second individual is a later non-founder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The tabular recursion for `i < j` with `j` a non-founder.

results.title: Tabular kinship when the second individual is a later founder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The tabular recursion for `i < j` with `j` a founder.

results.title: Tabular self-kinship of a non-founder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The tabular recursion on the diagonal for a non-founder: `φ i i = (1 + φ f m) / 2`.

results.title: Tabular self-kinship of a founder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The tabular recursion on the diagonal for a founder: `φ i i = 1 / 2`.

results.title: Tabular kinship when the first individual is a later non-founder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The tabular recursion for `j < i` with `i` a non-founder.

results.title: Tabular kinship when the first individual is a later founder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The tabular recursion for `j < i` with `i` a founder.

results.title: Symmetry of tabular kinship
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The tabular kinship is symmetric.

results.title: Ancestral paths from an individual
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The ancestral paths from `i`: the lists `[i = v₀, v₁, …, v_k]` with each `v_{t+1}` a parent of `v_t` (`k ≥ 0`; the path `[i]` has no edge).

results.title: Ancestral paths ending at a given ancestor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The ancestral paths from `i` that end at `A`.

results.title: Ancestral paths are nonempty with the starting individual as head
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every path in `ancPaths i` starts at `i` and is nonempty.

results.title: A founder gene copy is its own origin
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A founder copy is its own origin.

results.title: Origin of a gene copy of a non-founder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A copy of a non-founder descends from the chosen copy of the corresponding parent.

results.title: Ancestors precede their descendants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Ancestors precede their descendants.

results.title: Parents are ancestors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A parent is an ancestor.

results.title: A gene copy is identical by descent with itself
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two copies are identical by descent of themselves with probability `1`.

results.title: Symmetry of identity by descent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Identity by descent is symmetric.

results.title: Malécot's recursion step for identity by descent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: One step of Malécot's recursion for identity by descent.

results.title: Self-kinship under gene dropping
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `φ i i = (1 + F i) / 2` under gene dropping.

results.title: Founders are not inbred
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inbreeding coefficient of a founder is `0`.

results.title: Malécot
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inbreeding coefficient of `i` is the kinship of its parents, `F i = φ f m`, under gene dropping.

results.title: Malécot's recursion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Malécot's recursion under gene dropping: if `j ≠ i` is not an ancestor of `i` and has parents `f, m`, then `φ i j = (φ i f + φ i m) / 2`.

results.title: Zero kinship with an unrelated founder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A founder `j ≠ i` that is not an ancestor of `i` has kinship `0` with `i`.

results.title: Symmetry of gene-dropping kinship
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Gene-dropping kinship is symmetric.

results.title: Malécot's recursion computes gene-dropping kinship
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The kinship coefficient computed by Malécot's recursion is the probability of identity by descent under gene dropping.

results.title: Malécot's recursion computes the inbreeding coefficient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inbreeding coefficient computed by Malécot's recursion is the probability of identity by descent of the two copies of `i` under gene dropping.

results.title: Ancestral paths from a founder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The only ancestral path from a founder is `[i]`.

results.title: Ancestral paths from a non-founder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ancestral paths from a non-founder: `[i]` and `i :: q` for a path `q` from a parent.

results.title: Individuals on an ancestral path are its start or precede it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every individual on an ancestral path from `i` is `i` or precedes it.

results.title: Ancestral path as its start followed by a tail
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every ancestral path from `i` starts with `i`.

results.title: An ancestral path returning to its start is trivial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A path from `i` ending at `i` is `[i]`.

results.title: Trivial ancestral path
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `[i]` is an ancestral path from `i`.

results.title: Wright's path formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Wright's path formula in kinship form: `φ i j` is the sum, over common ancestors `A` (including `i` or `j` themselves) and pairs of ancestral paths `p` from `i` to `A` and `p'` from `j` to `A` that share no individual other than `A`, of `(1/2) ^ (n₁ + n₂ + 1) * (1 + F A)`, where `n₁ + n₂ + 1 = p.length + p'.length - 1` is the number of individuals on the loop.

results.title: Wright's path formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Wright's path formula for the inbreeding coefficient (Wright 1922): if `i` has parents `f = g 0` and `m = g 1`, then `F_i = Σ (1/2) ^ (n₁ + n₂ + 1) (1 + F_A)` over common ancestors `A` of `f` and `m` (including `f` or `m` themselves) and pairs of ancestral paths from `f` and `m` to `A` (with `n₁` and `n₂` edges) that share only `A`. Here `F` is the gene-dropping inbreeding coefficient.

results.title: Traveling-wave profile of the Fisher–KPP equation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `U` is a traveling-wave profile of speed `c` for `∂u/∂t = D ∂²u/∂x² + r u (1 - u)`: it is twice differentiable with first derivative `U'` and `U'' = -(c U' + r U (1 - U)) / D`, which for `D ≠ 0` is the profile equation `D U'' + c U' + r U (1 - U) = 0`.

results.title: Traveling front of the Fisher–KPP equation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A traveling front of speed `c`: a wave profile with `0 < U < 1`, `U → 1` at `-∞` and `U → 0` at `+∞`.

results.title: Time derivative of a traveling wave
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Time derivative of the wave `u(x, t) = U(x - c t)`: `∂u/∂t = -c U'(x - c t)`.

results.title: Space derivative of a traveling wave
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Space derivative of the wave: `∂u/∂x = U'(x - c t)`.

results.title: Traveling wave solves the Fisher–KPP equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Second space derivative of the wave; with `hD : D ≠ 0` it gives the PDE `-c U' = D U'' + r U (1 - U)`, i.e. `∂u/∂t = D ∂²u/∂x² + r u (1 - u)`.

results.title: No traveling wave with `c² < 4 r D`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `D, r > 0` and `c² < 4 r D`, a wave profile tending to `0` at `+∞` is not eventually positive. (This excludes `|c| < 2 √(r D)`, not `c < 2 √(r D)` for negative `c`.)

results.title: Minimal speed of Fisher–KPP traveling fronts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A front of speed `c` needs `c² ≥ 4 r D`; for `c ≥ 0` this is `c ≥ 2 √(r D)`.

results.title: Rate of the Ablowitz–Zeppetella wave
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The rate `κ = √(r / (6 D))` of the Ablowitz–Zeppetella wave.

results.title: Speed of the Ablowitz–Zeppetella wave
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Ablowitz–Zeppetella speed `c = 5 √(r D / 6)` (`5 / √6` when `D = r = 1`).

results.title: Ablowitz–Zeppetella wave profile
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Ablowitz–Zeppetella profile `U(z) = (1 + C exp (κ z))⁻²`.

results.title: Derivative of the Ablowitz–Zeppetella profile
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The derivative of the Ablowitz–Zeppetella profile, `-2 κ C e^{κ z} (1 + C e^{κ z})⁻³`.

results.title: The Ablowitz–Zeppetella front
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `D, r, C > 0`, `(1 + C exp (z √(r / (6 D))))⁻²` is a front of speed `5 √(r D / 6)`.

results.title: Ablowitz–Zeppetella speed exceeds the minimal front speed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Ablowitz–Zeppetella speed exceeds the minimal speed: `2 √(r D) < 5 √(r D / 6)`.

results.title: Kolmogorov–Petrovsky–Piskunov: fronts exist at every speed `c ≥ 2 √(r D)`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Kolmogorov–Petrovsky–Piskunov: fronts exist at every speed `c ≥ 2 √(r D)`, and they are strictly decreasing.
